o1.biggest_strength: Picks recruiting with the seat math in two lines, uses Priya's phrase, and puts security up with the demo button. Every section has its proof named.
o1.biggest_mistake: The A/B variants are two sides of the same idea (pain vs feature) rather than pain vs outcome, and the reminder section claims nothing beyond the data but still reads a little thin.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: A second hero that tests a genuinely different promise (e.g. outcome: 'fill your interview slots without chasing anyone') and one named, permissioned customer quote in the round robin section instead of a placeholder.

o2.biggest_strength: Nine sections with richer visuals, text/SMS reminders, reschedule-from-link, and a careful 'fill or cut' approach to facts it doesn't have.
o2.biggest_mistake: Too many CTAs alternate between 'Get started' and 'Book a demo' on a page aimed at teams, and a standalone open source section leads a recruiter away from the pain. Metrics are muddier (qualified team starts) than a clean demo-request rate.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut open source to a proof line, make every button 'Book a demo', trim to the owner's seven sections, and land on one clean deciding metric with a stop rule.

reason: Output 1 is the one I'd actually ship: segment math up front, security moved out of the footer, routing forms pulled up, and a deciding metric with a stop rule I can hand to the team. Output 2 has good detail but mixes its CTAs and buries open source in a section of its own where the recruiter doesn't need it.
